novelty_flags.label: thm:witness-separation
novelty_flags.one_line: Its consumer is only “a falsifiable diagnostic for whether a proposed covariance summary retains enough joint information,” with no named paper, bibkey, applied domain, or open problem.

novelty_flags.label: thm:open-neighborhood-separation
novelty_flags.one_line: Its consumer only says “The design recommendation survives small misspecification,” rather than naming a published workflow, applied validation domain, or unresolved problem.

soundness_flags.label: thm:local-chart-membership / q^0 localization
soundness_flags.one_line: q^0 in M_eta(p) permits q^0_axell=eta, so the stated negative local tilts need not remain in M_eta; add a declared strict slack condition min_axell(q^0_axell-eta)>0 (or lower eta) before asserting uniform local membership.

soundness_flags.label: r_alt^0 definition used by thm:witness-separation
soundness_flags.one_line: At omega_0 the asserted budget exhaustion is false: sum_{x,a} p_x e_ax r_alt,ax^0=0.53724, not B=0.55; r_alt^0 is still feasible, but the displayed justification must be corrected.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:deterministic-rate-limit and thm:local-minimax-lower-bound
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The comparison class excludes fully sequential acquisition, positive-fraction pilots, and random limiting annotation designs.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The minimax equality is claimed only for prospective procedures whose main-wave rates converge locally uniformly in probability to a deterministic feasible design after a vanishing pilot.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:certified-computation
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Certification assumes rational-polytopal state sets, rational or real-algebraic inputs, and exact validity certificates.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Termination and two-sided numerical certificates are claimed only on the explicitly represented domain I_rep, not for arbitrary real inputs or oracle-free compact sets.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: finite-support sampling model
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The LAN and implementation claims use fixed finite strata and known finite outcome support with positive annotation and outcome-cell floors.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The field-tier result is conditional on this finite-support prospective-annotation regime; continuous and binary-outcome extensions are outside the present claim.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The publication constructs a semiparametric Gaussian-sequence limit experiment for a scalar welfare contrast and transfers asymptotic Bayes/minimax treatment rules through a best regular estimator.

The paper studies two-wave experimental design for policy choice, uses Gaussian and quadratic approximations, and explicitly requires welfare to be strongly concave locally, ruling out binary treatment choice with linear welfare.

source_verification_receipts.locator: abstract and bibliographic record, lines 8-16 and 22-38
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The proceedings paper is titled Batch-Adaptive Causal Annotations and derives a closed-form batch sampling probability minimizing the asymptotic variance of a doubly robust ATE estimator with missing outcomes.
The paper optimizes semiparametric efficiency bounds for scalar parameters and gives a maximin construction for multi-dimensional parameters in two-phase sampling.
The paper derives near-minimax-regret allocation for Gaussian, separable subgroup treatment decisions, with allocation proportional to variance^(1/3) times subgroup weight^(2/3).
